reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 13 --verse 1.105.16: the evidence words stand verbatim in Sāyaṇa’s commentary on 1.105.16 (machine-checked against the packet). He says the Āditya cannot be overstepped even by the gods (atikramituṃ na śakyaḥ) because their life depends on it: with the Sun come the seasons, in the seasons the sacrifices, with the sacrifices the gods’ life; the sentence carries that chain and no more. Loosest point: Sāyaṇa makes panthāḥ an epithet of the Sun (satatagāmī, or the way of worshippers to Brahma’s world by the Sun’s gate), so what is not overstepped is the Sun himself; ‘a road’ follows the verse and his second gloss, not a drift into another reading. Wilson note c reports the same dependence. Plain sense checked against day.js: 1.105 is a refrain lament (‘Mark this my woe’), Trita in the well at 1.105.17; no four words of the key repeated. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.105.16, at [104,16]); entry-check ok, 45 words, at the cap. No school, comparison or tone issue.
